aspects.says: A stand-in or offline approval reaches the issuer as an advice or a clearing record, and the issuer applies it as if it had approved it, even when the account goes below zero.
basis: section:7.4. A Decision Taken Elsewhere Arrives as an Advice, and the Issuer Must Apply It
section:7.4.1. Spot the Problem: The Advice Nobody Recorded

aspects.says: In the dual-message flow an approval only holds the money; the clearing record posts the final amount and releases the whole hold, and without it the hold lapses and the merchant is never paid.
basis: section:7.2. An Approval Holds the Money in the Dual-Message Flow and Moves It in the Single-Message Flow

aspects.says: A payment crosses merchant, acquirer, network and issuer; only the issuer decides, and each hop is its own link, so only what the next link's specification defines gets across.
basis: section:7.1. A Payment Crosses Four Parties, and Each Hop Is a Link of Its Own

aspects.says: Settlement moves one net amount per institution for the settlement day, so no purchase appears in a transfer of its own, and 05xx messages agree totals without moving money.
basis: section:7.3. Settlement Moves One Net Amount per Institution, Days After the Purchases

aspects.says: Approvals that never reach clearing move no money: the cardholder is not charged and the merchant is not paid.
basis: section:7.2. An Approval Holds the Money in the Dual-Message Flow and Moves It in the Single-Message Flow

aspects.says: A reversal undoes a transaction only while it is open; once cleared, it is undone by a refund from the merchant or a chargeback from the issuer through the network's dispute process.
basis: section:7.5. What Undoes a Transaction Depends on How Far It Has Gone
